about.title: About the Project
about.subtitle: Context and Rationale
about.contextP1: Individuals with severe mental illness (SMI) continue to experience significantly lower employment rates compared to the general population, despite their willingness and capacity to work. While Supported Employment has proven effective in improving access to the open labour market, existing models often lack mental health-informed strategies that are essential for long-term job retention, workplace adaptation, and sustainable inclusion.
about.contextP2: MIND-SET addresses this gap by strengthening the Supported Employment model through Augmented Supported Employment (ASE), integrating mental health-oriented interventions that support both job placement and long-term employment sustainability. The project is implemented in Portugal and Romania within the framework of Erasmus+ KA210-VET.
about.approach1Text: Expanding the traditional Supported Employment model with mental health-informed strategies for sustainable employment outcomes.
about.approach2Text: Developing comprehensive training content integrating coaching techniques, workplace adaptation strategies, and employer engagement tools.
about.approach3Text: Creating practical resources for personalised employment planning, workplace adaptations, and stigma reduction.
about.approach4Text: Implementing the project across Portugal and Romania to ensure transferability and broader impact.
about.frameworkText: MIND-SET is funded under the Erasmus+ Programme, specifically the KA210-VET action for Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training. This European funding enables us to develop and deliver high-quality resources that benefit Supported Employment professionals and individuals with severe mental illness.
about.focusValue: Small-scale partnerships in vocational education and training

objectives.title: Objectives
objectives.subtitle: What we aim to achieve through the MIND-SET project
objectives.generalText: The general objective of MIND-SET is to strengthen vocational education and training and employment support services by advancing Augmented Supported Employment (ASE) as a mental health-informed approach that improves access to, retention in, and sustainability of employment for individuals with severe mental illness (SMI).
objectives.specific1Text: To develop and implement Augmented Supported Employment training content for Supported Employment consultants, integrating mental health-informed coaching techniques, workplace adaptation strategies, and employer engagement tools.
objectives.specific2Text: To enhance the professional capacity of Supported Employment professionals to provide long-term, tailored support to individuals with severe mental illness, with a focus on job retention and workplace inclusion.
objectives.specific3Text: To promote Augmented Supported Employment as an innovative and transferable best practice within vocational education and training and employment support services.
objectives.specific4Text: To raise employer awareness and preparedness regarding inclusive recruitment practices, reasonable workplace accommodations, and mental health-friendly work environments.
objectives.specific5Text: To contribute to the reduction of stigma and discrimination related to mental health in the labour market by fostering more informed, supportive, and inclusive workplaces.
objectives.impactText1: Through its integrated approach, MIND-SET enables Supported Employment professionals to strengthen their skills, supports employers in creating inclusive workplaces, and contributes to removing employment barriers for individuals with severe mental illness.
objectives.impactText2: By leveraging innovative methodologies aligned with evidence-based practices, MIND-SET aims to create lasting positive change in how individuals with severe mental illness are supported in accessing and maintaining employment across Europe.

targetGroups.title: Target Groups
targetGroups.subtitle: Who the MIND-SET project supports and serves
targetGroups.introText: The MIND-SET project aims to improve employment access, retention, and sustainability for individuals with severe mental illness by strengthening the capacity of Supported Employment services and vocational education and training systems in Portugal and Romania. To achieve this, several key target groups are directly and indirectly involved throughout the project.
targetGroups.primaryText: Supported Employment professionals, including job coaches, vocational counsellors, rehabilitation counsellors, social workers, and career advisors, are the primary target group of the MIND-SET project. The project focuses on strengthening their professional competencies by providing Augmented Supported Employment methodologies that integrate mental health-informed strategies, enabling them to deliver more effective, tailored, and long-term employment support.
targetGroups.secondary1Text: Individuals with severe mental illness, such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, and severe anxiety disorders, are the main beneficiaries of the project's outcomes. Through improved professional practices, they benefit from more personalised employment pathways, appropriate workplace adaptations, and strengthened job retention support in the open labour market.
targetGroups.secondary2Text: Employers and human resources professionals are engaged within the project to support inclusive recruitment practices, reasonable workplace accommodations, and the development of mental health-friendly work environments, contributing to more supportive and sustainable workplaces.
targetGroups.secondary3Text: Vocational education and training providers are involved to facilitate the integration of Augmented Supported Employment approaches into training pathways for employment professionals, reinforcing innovation and quality within vocational education and training systems.
targetGroups.secondary4Name: Policy Makers and Employment Service Providers
targetGroups.secondary4Text: Policy makers and employment service providers are addressed through the dissemination of project results and the promotion of Augmented Supported Employment as a best practice, supporting the uptake of evidence-based approaches in policies and programmes aimed at improving labour market inclusion for individuals with severe mental illness.
targetGroups.beneficiariesText: Through this integrated approach, MIND-SET strengthens the capacity of Supported Employment professionals, engages employers in inclusive and mental health-informed practices, and contributes to removing employment barriers for individuals with severe mental illness.

activities.title: Activities
activities.subtitle: What we are implementing in the MIND-SET project
activities.introText: The MIND-SET project is implemented through a set of interconnected activities designed to strengthen vocational education and training, enhance professional competencies in Supported Employment, and promote inclusive labour market practices for individuals with severe mental illness. Each activity contributes to the development, testing, and long-term sustainability of Augmented Supported Employment approaches.
activities.activity1Title: Augmented Supported Employment Toolkit: Advancing Mental Health Inclusion
activities.activity1Text:
This activity focuses on the development of the core project output: the Augmented Supported Employment Toolkit. The Toolkit expands the Supported Employment model by integrating mental health-informed strategies that support both job placement and long-term employment retention for individuals with severe mental illness.

The Toolkit includes practical resources for professionals, such as guidance on personalised employment planning, workplace adaptations, employer engagement, stigma reduction, and access to complementary support services. All resources are developed collaboratively by the project partners and made available in digital format.
activity1List: All resources developed collaboratively and available in digital format
activities.activity2Title: Advancing Professional Competencies in Augmented Supported Employment
activities.activity2Text:
This activity pilots and validates the Augmented Supported Employment approach through blended training programmes delivered in Portugal and Romania. In total, eight training sessions (four per country) are organised, involving at least 28 Supported Employment professionals.

The activity includes pre- and post-training assessments and follow-up actions to evaluate the application of Augmented Supported Employment methodologies in real work settings.
activity2List: Evaluation of ASE methodologies in real work settings
activities.activity3Title: Scaling and Sustaining Augmented Supported Employment
activities.activity3Text:
This activity focuses on dissemination, exploitation, and sustainability, ensuring that the project's results reach a wide audience and remain accessible beyond the project's duration.

Key actions include the organisation of two national multiplier events (one in Portugal and one in Romania), dissemination through digital channels, and the promotion of Augmented Supported Employment as a best practice. The project website will remain available for at least five years after project completion.
activity3List: Two national multiplier events (Portugal and Romania)
Promotion of ASE as a best practice
Project website available for at least five years after completion
activities.method1Text: Involving professionals and stakeholders throughout the development process to ensure resources meet real needs.
activities.method2Text: Building on proven Supported Employment methodologies and integrating mental health-informed strategies.
activities.method3Text: Leveraging digital tools to maximise accessibility, reach, and long-term availability of resources.
activities.method4Text: Implementing rigorous testing and validation processes to ensure high-quality outputs.
activities.conclusionText: Through these activities, MIND-SET supports innovation in vocational education and training, strengthens professional practice in Supported Employment, and promotes more inclusive and sustainable employment pathways for individuals with severe mental illness.

results.title: Results
results.subtitle: Outputs and impact of the MIND-SET project
results.introText: The MIND-SET project delivers concrete outputs and generates meaningful impact by strengthening vocational education and training, enhancing Supported Employment practice, and promoting inclusive labour market participation for individuals with severe mental illness.
results.result1Text: A dedicated project website serving as a central digital repository for all MIND-SET outputs, ensuring structured access to resources, transparency of results, and long-term availability beyond the project's duration.
results.result2Text: A comprehensive Augmented Supported Employment Toolkit that expands the Supported Employment model by integrating mental health-informed strategies. The Toolkit provides practical guidance for professionals on personalised employment planning, workplace adaptations, employer engagement, stigma reduction, and access to complementary support services.
results.result3Title: Blended Training Programme for Supported Employment Professionals
results.result3Text: A structured blended training programme implemented in Portugal and Romania, supporting the professional development of Supported Employment practitioners. The programme combines interactive sessions, case-based learning, and practical application of Augmented Supported Employment methodologies.
results.result4Text: National and joint pilot and follow-up reports documenting the testing and validation of the Augmented Supported Employment approach in real work settings. These reports capture evidence, lessons learned, and good practices, supporting the refinement and transferability of the methodology.
results.result5Text: Two national multiplier events, organised in Portugal and Romania, presenting the project's methodology, resources, and results to professionals, organisations, and relevant stakeholders, supporting dissemination and uptake at national level.
results.impact1Text: By equipping professionals with structured tools and mental health-informed methodologies, MIND-SET improves the quality and effectiveness of Supported Employment services for individuals with severe mental illness.
results.impact2Text: The project contributes to more sustainable employment pathways by addressing mental health-related barriers, supporting workplace adaptations, and strengthening long-term job retention in the open labour market.
results.impact3Text: Through targeted resources and engagement, MIND-SET supports increased employer awareness of inclusive recruitment practices, reasonable workplace accommodations, and mental health-friendly work environments.
results.impact4Title: Innovation in Vocational Education and Training
results.impact4Text: By promoting Augmented Supported Employment as a transferable best practice, the project contributes to innovation and quality improvement within vocational education and training systems and employment support services.
results.impact5Text: Project resources remain accessible through the project website and partner communication channels, supporting continued use, adaptation, and dissemination beyond the project's lifetime.

partners.title: Partners
partners.subtitle: A transnational partnership for mental health inclusion
partners.introText: The MIND-SET project is implemented by a transnational partnership bringing together organisations with complementary expertise in vocational education and training, Supported Employment, mental health inclusion, and employment services. The partnership combines practical field experience with training capacity and policy-oriented perspectives to ensure high-quality results and sustainable impact.
partners.partner1Name: RUMO, Cooperativa de Solidariedade Social, Crl
partners.partner1Text: RUMO, Cooperativa de Solidariedade Social, Crl, is a non-profit organisation founded in 1981 and based in Barreiro, Portugal. Its mission is to promote the educational, professional, and community inclusion of disadvantaged individuals within the framework of the Supported Employment movement. As a founding member of the Portuguese Association of Supported Employment, RUMO has extensive experience in vocational training, labour market integration, and support for vulnerable groups, including people with disabilities or impairments and individuals with severe mental illness.
partners.partner1Text2: Networking and partnership development are central to RUMO's work, as collaboration is essential for effective and sustainable inclusion practices. The organisation works closely with employers, public institutions, civil society organisations, vocational training centres, and self-advocacy groups to promote inclusive employment, raise awareness of the rights of disadvantaged individuals and those at risk of social exclusion, and provide support for labour market integration and professional training.
partners.partner2Text: CONSULTIS is a Portuguese company established in 2005 and headquartered in Vila Nova de Gaia, specialising in business consultancy, innovation, and Supported Employment. As an active member of the Portuguese Association of Supported Employment, it operates a Resource Centre in Porto, supporting employers, professionals, and jobseekers, with a particular focus on groups facing disadvantage in the labour market, including disabled individuals and other people at risk of social exclusion. CONSULTIS plays a key role in advancing methodological innovation within Supported Employment practice.
partners.partner2Text2: Working in partnership with businesses, training entities, educational institutions, social organisations, and public bodies, CONSULTIS develops tailored solutions that respond to labour market needs and promote inclusive employment practices. Through its consultancy services, training programmes, and Supported Employment initiatives, the organisation supports employers and professionals in implementing inclusive and sustainable employment solutions.
partners.partner3Text: Health Action Overseas Romania (HAO) is a non-governmental organisation active in Romania since 1991, specialising in community-based social services for children, young people, and adults with disabilities in Constanța, Galați, and Bucharest. Initially focused on supporting children with severe disabilities in residential institutions, HAO has expanded its work to include educational and therapeutic programmes, supported living arrangements, community development, advocacy, and family support.
partners.partner3Text2: HAO provides Supported Employment services for young adults with disabilities, including individuals with severe mental illness, and is active in the field of Vocational Education and Training (VET). The organisation develops capacity-building programmes that promote social, civic, and professional skills and delivers specialised training for professionals involved in the social and professional inclusion of disabled individuals, ensuring the application of effective, person-centred methodologies.
